utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. And what was his function back in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, this witness calls for no cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'll just try to put a few questions in view of the fact that this witness did not mention Dragan Jokic, apart from the last part of this testimony, so I would like to clarify this misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, witness?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to attempt to clarify the answer you gave before the last one. When asked by the Prosecutor as to whether you knew what Dragan Jokic's duty was, you said that he was the commander of a company or battalion of engineers in the Zvornik Brigade. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What duty he performed and what his place was in the chain of command, I don't know. Whether he was the commander of the chief of the engineers' unit, I'm not sure, but it was the entire engineers' unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will try to deal with this. The Zvornik Brigade had an engineers' company in its composition. According to what we know, the commander of the engineers' company was Dragan Jevtic. While Dragan Jokic was the chief of the engineering branch in the command of the Zvornik Brigade, Dragan Jokic was the chief and not the commander. I'm asking whether I'm right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think the witness gave his answer and what counsel now does is try to correct his answer. Does he have a question for him or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, you could ask a question concerning of the position of Mr. Jokic at that time, but you cannot furnish the answer in your question. Please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. To be quite honest, I don't understand the Prosecutor's position. With the best of intentions, I am trying to clarify something that I think is not in dispute. So I don't know why they had to object. If they don't care about clarifying this misunderstanding, I will not continue this line of questioning. Please allow me to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, we'll take whatever the witness told us. You know, what the witness testified in this courtroom may have multipurpose. There may be evidence against your client or not, or they may test about his own credibilities in the future. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I will continue my examination, concentrating on areas of interest to us. You said that sometime between 11.00 and 12.00, you received a telephone call from the brigade, because the battalion commander was absent at the moment from the battalion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that this telephone call arrived from the duty officer in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what my duty officer in the battalion told me, that the duty officer from the brigade was on the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's just what I wanted to ask you. Does this mean that the man you talked to did not introduce himself to you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Not as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As we are speaking the same language, please wait for the interpreter to finish interpreting my question before you reply. Thank you. You also said today that you knew Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you assist us by saying whether you talked to Dragan Jokic on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I've already said that it was the duty officer from the brigade. And who the duty officer was, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand you don't even know whether it was the duty officer. This was what your duty officer in the battalion told you. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but who was actually on duty on that day, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that the brigade command in mid-July 1995 had its forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where this forward command post of the brigade was?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the forward command post of the brigade was in Kitovnice and the location, the precise location, I don't know, but it was in the village of Kitovnice or Parlog.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were there duty officers at the forward command post at the time, in view of the combat situation?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean from the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any communication with the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean from the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Specifically, was there a line of communication between the forward command post and the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think there was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I would just like to clarify. The witness had asked whether he meant the forward command post of the battalion or from the brigade. And at least on the transcript it has not been clarified, so I'm not sure which communication between him and the forward command post is meant now. The forward command post of the brigade or the battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's not very clear in the transcript. Mr. Stojanovic, would you please ask some questions to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question was: In this period, was there a line of communication between the brigade forward command post and the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There was, because from the forward command post they had communications with the brigade and through there to the battalion command or the command of all the battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's precisely why I asked this question. At the time when your duty officer in the battalion said: You have the duty officer from the brigade on the line, is it possible for this information to go from the duty officer at the forward command post through the brigade to the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it's possible or not. I was told that it was the duty officer from the brigade who was calling, probably whoever was on duty at the brigade would know this. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that you don't know this. You couldn't have known, but I ask you: In view of what you said at the beginning, that as the deputy commander you had information of communication lines -- about communication lines. My question is: Would you allow for such a possibility as regards the system of communication?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I've already said that in the battalion I took care of the communication line, making sure it was operational, making sure that we had good communications with the companies at the frontline and with the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will just repeat my question once again. Is it possible, and please say yes or no or I don't know, that a call should come from the duty officer at the forward command post through the duty communications officer in the brigade to the duty communications officer in your battalion. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know. Perhaps yes, but I can't be sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion between 11.00 and 12.00, did you speak to the man whom you were told was the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you be able to tell us, to the extent that you were familiar with Dragan Jokic and his voice whether this could have been his voice or not, or can't you answer?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember the voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At one point you said that there was more than one commanding officer in the command. What did you mean by that? What command question -- the brigade command, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There was more than one commanding officer there because they had good communications, good rears, and there was more than one officer there. Which of them was on duty on that day, I wouldn't know. The person who drew up the roster in the brigade would be able to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that in that period of time from 11.00 to 12.00, it was to be expected that there would be more than one officer present in the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know which of the commanding officers were in the brigade command at that time. Probably -- of course it was possible that more than one officer would be there, but whether that actually happened on that day, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How well did you know Drago Nikolic at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I've already said that for about seven months I was in the 1st Battalion, I think, as assistant commander for security within the battalion, and that was when I got to know Drago Nikolic. I didn't him before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that on that morning a meeting was held in the command of the Zvornik Brigade which was attended by security officers from the battalion and from the brigade and that the meeting was concluded before noon?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that on that occasion you talked to Drago Nikolic about the fact that prisoners would be arriving in a few hours and that they should go to the school?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It was the duty officer from the brigade who told me this. I've already told you I don't know who it was. I really don't know whether it was Drago Nikolic or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I understood you to say that you expected that these prisoners would be in the school for a time and that after that they would be exchanged. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That was my personal opinion, my personal opinion. It was just an opinion, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What did you base this opinion on?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I've already said that in 1993 or 1994 our soldiers captured a member of the Muslim army up there on the front line. They brought him to us at the command. Then he was taken to the Zvornik Brigade, where I don't know whether he was interrogated or not. But I'm sure that after a certain time, this man was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that why you thought that these people who were to be brought to the school would also be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely this. That's why I thought they would be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: May I conclude from your reply that in the conversation you had between 11.00 and 12.00, you were not told what would happen to these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I've already said that I was told the prisoners would be arriving. As to what would happen to them, nobody said anything about that at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "at that time" --

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I mean when the duty officer from the brigade called me between 11.00 and 12.00. He said that these prisoners would be arriving and that they would be put up in the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And at that time, nobody said what would then happen to the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Nobody told me anything. They just told me where they would be put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did someone then tell you at some other time what would happen to these prisoners, and did you have any other knowledge as to what would happen to them?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the indictment that we have before us it says that on the 15th in the early morning hours, the burial of the victims began at the Petkovci dam. My question to you is: As the deputy commander of the battalion, are you personally aware of who took part in the burial of the victims?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No. That morning I went to the area of the 4th Company, where I stayed until late in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody ever tell you that on that morning machinery arrived at the Petkovci dam to bury the victims?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me, then, that there is practically no purpose in examining you further, because you know nothing about the burials?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about the burials.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And only one more question about this. On the 15th when you returned from the 4th Company and spent the time until 1.00 a.m. From the 15th to the 16th in the battalion command, did you see Dragan Jokic around anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will now try to clarify another point. Today you said that one of the two soldiers who were killed on that occasion by a shell was a soldier nicknamed -- whose last name was Micic. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you sure he was a member of the engineers' company?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the battalion, we had two members of the engineers' company, this Micic and another man whose first name was Milisav, and I can't remember his last name, and this Milisav was a school friend of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We have a list here of the members of the engineers' company, which has been exhibited -- it was exhibited when Mr. Butler testified. Can you help us by telling us the first name of this Micic so that we can check it on the list of the members of the engineers' company.

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember his first name exactly, but I know he was born in the village of Trsic that's all I know and his last name was Micic. The other man's first name was Milislav and his last name was Martinovic. But I can't remember his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's just clarify: Milisav Martinovic was not a member of the engineers' company?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He was in our battalion and he was a member of the engineers' company, he and this Micic who were killed, because they made sure that the frontline which was mined was kept in good order, and that if a mine exploded, it should be replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now we understand each other. Am I right in saying that these two soldiers were resubordinated and they served in the 6th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were in the 6th Battalion on behalf of the engineers' company, and they worked with us in the matters that had to do with the engineering matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we have clarified this. And let's try and deal with another thing. Are you aware of the fact the chief of engineers in the command of the brigade, and this specialty or this formation, is it separate from the commander of the engineers' company? Are these two different things?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the chief of engineers is different from the commander, and that the commander is probably subordinated to the chief of engineers, like the commander of the company in my battalion was subordinated to the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well then. I wanted to ask you: Do you have military training or education?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. I said that at the beginning. I told you what my profession was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, you said that after the compulsory military service you were given the rank of a lance corporal?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, from the Army of the then-Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question is: Are these two functions separate and do they exist separately, one, the chief of engineers, and the other, commander of engineers?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact answer [Realtime transcript read in error "number"].

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I wanted to ask you a few more things that have to do with your acquaintance with Dragan Jokic and your views of his character. How closely did you socialise at that time with Dragan Jokic and how closely did you know him?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. During that period, because I understand that you arrived from Kladanj, so let's say between 1992 and 1996, until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We did not socialise. We just saw each other if I had to go to the brigade, and then I would see him there by chance, because I was on a different side. I was in the command of the 6th Battalion. So we saw each other rather rarely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sinatra. Is there a problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There is a problem in the transcript that means a lot to the definition of the answers for the witness. On -- at 20.17.04.26, the transcript says: I can't give you the exact number and the witness said I can't give you the exact answer. And that's a big difference in his testimony before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And I believe the interpreter had corrected herself orally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But it's not reflected in the transcript. Maybe, Mr. Stojanovic, we could go over that again to make sure, since Ms. Sinatra claims that is very important to your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may repeat the question, we will surely get the right answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question was: The functions of the chief of engineers and the commander of the engineering company, are they two separate functions?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I said I couldn't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I bring my cross-examination to an end, Your Honour, because we have received the answer to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was your impression of Dragan Jokic's character, in view of the level of acquaintance you had with him at that period?

utterances.speaker: MARKO MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I believe that he was an honest man, a man of integrity.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honours. Thank you, and I would like to thank the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect, Mr. Waespi?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, at this stage, are there any documents to tender? Mr. Waespi?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It's the sketch drawn by the witness himself, Exhibit P668.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we are talking about a map rather than a drawing, and this could lead to a misunderstanding. So if we are talking about the map, we don't have any objections to the map being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I do apologise. The reference I wanted to make is that he added, you know, some marks on to that map. But it's a map, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So there is no disputes about it. So this document is admitted into the evidence. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. I think during the break the usher will pull down the blinds and show you out of the room. And we all wish you a pleasant journey back home. We will have our break and we will resume at 20 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good evening, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good evening, sir. Can you -- perhaps we can start off by you stating your name for the record and spelling your last name, please.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: S-t-a-n-o-j-e-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay, and that's your last name, it's Mr. Stanojevic?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: O-s-t-o-j-a.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I take it that was your first name?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you and I met, I believe it was yesterday, you were given your rights to counsel and your right to remain silent. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you waived those rights and agreed to speak to us without counsel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you have agreed to testify today without the presence of counsel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Perhaps we can start off with some background information, sir. Can you tell us what your date of birth is.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: 13 August, 1947.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And what is your educational background, just very briefly?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I finished elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And I understand, sir, that your ethnicity is Serbian. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you were serving in the army, the Bosnian Serb army, during the course of the war, from 1992 until the end of the war. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what branch of the army have you been serving in?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Engineers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when did you join the engineering branch?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: 23rd June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what were your duties at that time?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I was a driver.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And during the period of July 1995, which unit were you serving in?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Engineers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what brigade is that?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: The Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Who was your immediate commander at the time?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Major Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is that Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Dragan, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And do you see Mr. Jokic in the courtroom today?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Can you just point him out for the record and briefly describe what he's wearing.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: He's sitting to my left, and he's wearing a suit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, and for the record, he's just identified the accused Dragan Jokic. And what about the other drivers of the engineering unit, sir, to whom did they report?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Major Jokic. And there are also platoon commanders there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And where was the engineering unit located?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: In Karakaj across the road from Glinica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And where was Major Jokic's office located in relation to your location, the engineering unit?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: It was within the same compound.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Now, in July of 1995, were you assigned to a particular vehicle?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And can you describe that vehicle for us.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: It was FAP 1921, it was a Kip truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what capacity does this truck have?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: 8 tonnes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was there anyone else who was using the truck besides yourself?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: If I wasn't there, then there were other people who could use it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And by "other people," are you referring to other drivers in your unit?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Turning, then, specifically, sir, to July of 1995, could you name the officers at the engineering unit.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Major Jokic and Dragan Jevtic, who was his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And who did you receive instructions from directly?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Either from Major Jokic or from commanders.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in what manner were instructions given to you?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Orally. They told us what we had to do orally.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Most of the time, sir, who did you receive instructions from?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: The platoon commanders and Major Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on 14 July of 1995, what were your duties that day?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: It was a Friday, I think. In the morning when Major Jokic arrived at about 9.00, he was in the command of the staff and he told me to get the car ready and that I would spend several days in the field. He said I was to go to Srebrenica to clear up some garbage that was there and that I was to report to the civilian protection in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, just to clarify, sir, we had -- it was translated as a car that you had to get ready. Can you tell us specifically the type of vehicle that you had to get ready.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: The F-a-p, Fap Kiper, 1921.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And did you follow those instructions?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So after having received that instruction from Major Jokic, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I went to Zvornik. I reported to the civilian protection there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what happened when you reported to the civil defence in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: They told me to wait. I waited for maybe an hour and a half. Then three people came, Dragan Mirkovic, Rajko Djokic, and Arsen Krunic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where did you wait?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: In front of the civilian protection building in the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what were you wearing when you reported to them?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: A military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. What happened after you waited?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Nothing happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did they come back and speak to you at any time, those three individuals that you told us about?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: They told me to wait, and then we went to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And who did you go to Bratunac with?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Rajko Djokic and Arsen Krunic were with me in the truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where was Dragan Mirkovic?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: He took his own car.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And when you arrived at Bratunac, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I parked the truck by the church in Bratunac. The two of them went to the municipality building, and that is where they found Dragan, who was already there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that -- you're referring to Dragan Mirkovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And did they say anything to you or did they -- at some point? Did they come back and give you instructions?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: They told me to wait there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And after they went into the municipal building, did they return at some point?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, after having stayed there for a longer time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what did they say to you after they came out of the building? What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: They came up to my truck and told me that Dragan Mirkovic and Krunic were to go home, and that Rajko was to stay with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did Rajko tell you what you were to do next, what were your next instructions?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: We spent the night in the hotel. And on the following morning, we were to go to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And which hotel was that?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I am not that familiar with Bratunac. I only know that there was one hotel in the centre. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And when did you get your next instructions?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: After breakfast, I went up to my truck and Rajko went to the municipal building. I didn't see him until that evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And are you now referring to the following morning after you spent the night in the hotel?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And I just want to ask you about the time. You said you had your breakfast, and did you meet with Rajko that morning?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He went to the municipality building.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And when did he return again to see you?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what the time was. It was around noon. He told me that we still couldn't go to Srebrenica. He didn't tell me why. He only told me to continue waiting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you meet with anybody else around that time?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did anyone else give you any instructions during that day?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And who was that?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: A man came, a worker probably from the civilian protection, but I don't know. He told me to go to Kravica to do something, according to somebody's orders. I don't know who the orders were from.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And did you go to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you go alone or did you go with anyone?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know the road, so he told me he would go with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Did you -- do you know this man's name?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you describe him?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can't describe him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Was there anyone else with you besides this gentleman when you went to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you indicate what this gentleman was wearing.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: He had civilian clothes, working clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what route did you take to get to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: We went towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And at this stage, sir, were you able to call Major Jokic and tell him what was happening?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not able to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Because the question suggests that the gentleman was requested to call Major Jokic, and I think it's misleading, the question itself. It's almost like asking somebody: When did you stop beating your wife? That sort of a question. So I object to the line of -- the way the question was phrased and the answer that was solicited. It's improper, unless you can lay a foundation that at some point that day he was supposed to call Major Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. But we have already passed that section, and the witness has answered that question. He said he was not able to do that. But I hope Ms. Issa could be careful in the future in the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. I would have submissions to make on this point, subject to Your Honour, but I will follow Your Honour's instructions on this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you arrived at Kravica, can you describe what you saw?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I found a truck there full of human corpses. There was an excavator that loaded bodies on to the truck. There was some six people there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Can you describe the place where they were loading bodies.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was close to a building in front of a garage. There was some distance between the garage and the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Well, turning, then, to Prosecution Exhibit P10.1. I'm going to ask you -- I'm going to show you a photograph, sir, and ask you if you recognise it.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. So can you tell us what this photograph depicts.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is the garage, the second building here, where corpses were, and they were loaded on to my truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Could you point to that.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So it's the second garage from the left side of the photograph. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So for the record, Your Honour, I think he's referring to the second garage from the left side of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, around what time of day was this, sir?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And how many people did you see loading bodies?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Five people.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Can you describe the manner in which they were loading the bodies.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: There was an excavator in front of the garage door. They were bringing bodies out, and they loaded the bodies into the grab. And when the grab was full, then that grab would load the bodies into my truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Can you indicate whether or not they were physically taking the bodies out with their hands or was it the excavator that was taking out the bodies. Can you clarify that.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: The bodies were being taken out from the garage by the excavator; the excavator did that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what were the men doing with the bodies?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You just described to us whether or not -- let me ask you this: Were the men touching the bodies? I'm sorry, I didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I could see them taking them out of the building. I was standing by the other building, close to my truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And how many bodies did you see being placed in that truck?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. They threw in two grab-fulls of bodies. I don't know how many bodies could one excavator grab hold at a time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Are you able to describe the size of the excavator, its dimensions?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know its dimensions, but I'm sure that it was 2 metres wide and that it could hold about 1 to 1.5 cubic metres of sand.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And was the truck that you saw filled to its capacity?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many bodies approximately you saw in the truck?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't really look, and I couldn't really see. I didn't stand up in my truck cab in order to see how many bodies there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And where were you located in relation to the truck, the other truck?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: The other truck was not there. The truck that I saw had already left, and I was there on my own.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So did you see that truck that you saw leave? Did you see it depart?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw it leaving.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And after it left, sir, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I parked in front of that building so my truck could be loaded. That's what I was told to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who told you that? Who gave you that instruction?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: That man who came with me all the way from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to show you a diagram, turning then to Prosecution Exhibit 670, with the assistance of Mr. Usher, and I'm going to ask you if you can identify it for us.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: This is the road that I came down from. This is where I was. This is the building. These are garages, and this is where the excavator was in front of the door. And this is the Kravica/Bratunac road.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So for the record the letters K and B refer to the Kravica/Bratunac road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where you pointed, where it's marked -- the letter D, that is the location where the excavator was loading bodies. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And where were you located, sir?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I was by the building. I was drinking water as they were loading the bodies. Then I went to the truck, and when they loaded the second batch, two men went with me to our destination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we're going to get to the second batch. I'm now going to ask you, sir, where you were -- well, let me ask you this first of all. Were bodies loaded into your truck?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Where were you when the bodies were loaded into your truck?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I was up there, the end of the building. I was drinking water. As they were loading the first batch, I was there drinking water. As they were loading the second batch, I was in the truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So let's talk about the first batch for the time being, and can you point to where you were in the diagram when they were loading the first batch. If you look at the diagram on the overhead projector, sir, next to you on your left, and point to it, please.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: This is where I was at the far end of the building. I was drinking water here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So that's around where it's marked the letter C, for the record. Okay.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how many bodies did they load into your truck?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. How many bucket-fulls did they load in your truck?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Two bucket-fulls.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And were the bodies loaded into your truck in the same manner as they had loaded the bodies in the previous truck?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how they loaded the first truck. It was already ready to leave, so I suppose they did it in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us, sir, what was the capacity of the bucket?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't mean to object, but these questions have been asked already at least once if not twice, and the gentleman has already indicated -- so I understand she wants to get through this material, but the gentleman indicated before that he did not know how many bodies could fit in. He did give an approximation as to the size and as to the cubic metres of the bucket. So I don't want to belabour the point. This line of questioning has been asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I was simply trying to clarify a point and I think counsel has to be very careful as to what he says in front of the witness. I think that's very important, and I certainly try to be careful, and I think care should be taken in that regard. I think I asked a different question before. I was asking about the dimensions, and I'm trying to simply clarify the point if he knows. I don't believe it's repetitive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But this question sounds very similar to the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I don't disagree with Your Honour on that point, however it may lead to a more elaborate answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Or rather --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's try that, yes. Can you ask your question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us, sir, the capacity of the bucket, just approximately from what you saw?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: 1.5 cubic metres of gravel or sand, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'll leave the point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you describe, sir, what the clothing was on the bodies? What were the bodies wearing?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you see any injuries on the bodies?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't come any closer to them. I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you speak to any of the men loading the bodies into your truck?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you speak to the person who was driving the loader or the excavator?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the men that were working with the bodies, what were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Civilian clothes, working clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you say "working clothes," can you describe more specifically what they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Blue uniforms, such as worn by people who are in civilian protection or people employed in public utilities companies, that kind of clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, was your truck filled to its capacity with bodies?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Approximately how many bodies were in your truck?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you give us an approximation, sir?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Can you describe what the loader looked like?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The loader had four wheels. It had one bucket in the front part, and this was a bucket that would normally be used for loading gravel.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Turning, then, to Prosecution Exhibit P63.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you've seen this photograph when you and I met. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And looking at this photograph, can you indicate what the loader looked like in relation to this photograph.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: It was similar to this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Was it different in any way?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. It may have been a little lower, and the bucket was perhaps smaller and a little lower down.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after the bodies were loaded into your truck, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I went with those two workers so that they would tell me where I would unload these bodies, and we drove in the direction of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Which two workers did you go with?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: The one who came with me from Bratunac and another one who worked on the loading.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And can you describe the direction that you went in on your way to Glogova.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So turning, then, to another diagram, Exhibit Number 669. Do you recognise this diagram, sir?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who drew the diagram? Do you know who drew the diagram?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Is that your signature on the bottom?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you indicate what this diagram depicts using the pointer?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: You can see the house and the grave below the house, and this is the main road and this is where I turned off the main road. And beneath this house was a grave. It wasn't far from the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. So for the record, the letters K and B refer to the road, and the letter D refers to the house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the letters E and C depicts the grave. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, not C. The letter E only depicts the grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how many pits did you see when you arrived or graves?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: There was only one.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see anyone there at the grave when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, only the two workers who came and who remained there later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see any bodies inside the grave when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There were bodies inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you do when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: The grave had been dug, and there was a gentle slope. So with the help of the two workers, I went into reverse gear so that they could unload.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Can you describe how the bodies were unloaded from your truck into the grave.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Those two workers climbed on to the truck. They opened the back, and then they threw the bodies out.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Where were you when the bodies were being thrown into the grave?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I was inside the truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What happened after the bodies were thrown into the grave?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I went back to Kravica, and the two of them remained there to wait for me because there were more bodies to be brought there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And who instructed you to return back to Kravica to bring back more bodies?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: They told me at Kravica -- when I set out, they told me there were more bodies to collect.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you returned to Kravica, can you describe what you did.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I parked the truck in the same place so they could load the remaining bodies on to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And how many bucket-fulls did they load this time?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Two, but there were fewer bodies than the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And after the bodies were loaded on to your truck this time, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I went back again to the same place in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you -- what did you do in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: To unload the bodies of the dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And how were they unloaded this time?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: In the same way as the first time. The two workers who had remained there climbed on to the truck and they piled up the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you do after the bodies were thrown into the pit a second time?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I went to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And where did you go in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I went and parked the truck in the same place, near the church.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you wash the truck off?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you meet with anyone that evening?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't know anyone in Bratunac. It was the first time I had been in that town.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I went to the hotel to sleep.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what did you do the next morning?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: After I had had breakfast, Rajko was there. He'd gone to the municipality, and we were supposed to go to Srebrenica. I was near the truck, and when I arrived he said that he had heard in the municipality that the military had come to the demarcation line the Baljkovica, that a lot of people had been killed, and we agreed that we should go to Zvornik and not to Srebrenica, where we were supposed to go on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And did you return to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you tell Rajko what you had been doing the previous day?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: When I passed through Kravica and went to Zvornik, I told him then where the bodies were.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And how did he respond?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you do when you arrived in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Rajko went to the civilian protection office, and I continued on to my barracks in the youth settlement where we were billeted. There I parked the truck and went home to hear from my family, because I had relatives at the demarcation line, and it was then that I learned that a cousin of mine had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: The next day did you report to anyone?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: On the next day?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean on Sunday when I arrived -- no the next day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Monday.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I went to the command, and I met Commander Jokic. And I asked him to let me go to Baljkovica to look for my cousin. No one had found him, and I think he granted my request and I went there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you tell Commander Jokic what you had been doing in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I told him I was unhappy about it, and he told me he had given me over to the civilian protection and that it was they who gave this order to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. To your knowledge, sir, would the civil defence send Major Jokic's instructions directly or would they have to go to the Zvornik Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Jokic couldn't have decided on this on his own. The brigade had to give them the truck and myself -- I mean, the civilian protection. It had to go through senior people.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may interject here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am told, I am told by Ms. Tomanovic that there might have been a slight mistake in the translation when the gentleman indicated what Mr. Jokic had told him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think you have the opportunity to cross-examine this witness to clarify this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What I'm saying is the gentleman said one thing and it was translated -- there was an omission in the translation. That's what I'm stating, Your Honour. So perhaps -- and I don't want to -- for the sake of the record if the gentleman could be asked a question and maybe given an opportunity to give the answer again. That's all I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, that's a reasonable request. Ms. Issa, could you please ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right, sir, could you tell us again about reporting to Mr. Jokic regarding what you did at Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: He told me then that he hadn't sent me to do that job, but the civilian protection ordered me to do this. I was supposed to go to Srebrenica to drive garbage. I was supposed to stay there for another 15 days. There was quite a lot of work to be done, but he didn't know about what I was doing. I was not happy that I had done this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever report to anyone else, aside from Major Jokic, about the bodies that you saw in Kravica and the grave in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. Only Rajko knew and Major Jokic. I didn't tell anyone else about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Why not? Why didn't you tell anyone else about it?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't, I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you ask anyone why there were bodies at Kravica, where they came from?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. There was no one to ask. I didn't know anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you ask the people, the men that were loading bodies at the time, or the worker that you went with?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I just have one more exhibit, sir, to show you. Exhibit 517, which is taken from the Zvornik Brigade vehicle log. Now, you have had an opportunity to look at this vehicle log when you and I met. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you see your name there listed as a driver that went to Orahovac on the 14th of July and to Kozluk on the 16th of July? Your name is there on those two occasions?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No -- yes, my name is here on the travel order, but this is a TAM 75; that was a luxury vehicle in our view. It's possible that I filled it with fuel the first time and they filled this in my name. And then they could fill it with fuel without me sitting behind the wheel for a whole month, so this is actually not relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So just to clarify, you're saying -- did you go to the -- you did not go to those places, to Orahovac and Kozluk on those dates?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours, this witness calls for no cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, we have less than 15 minutes left. Do you prefer to do your cross tomorrow or do you prefer to start right now?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as I think it will last longer than a quarter of an hour, it might be better if we left it for tomorrow, if Your Honour doesn't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But can you give me some indication how long your cross will last, just approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think half an hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, Witness, I have to remind you that you are under the oath, so do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony tonight and tomorrow morning. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And I think the hearing is adjourned, and we'll resume at 11.30 in this courtroom tomorrow morning.
